question: Should OpenClaw accept `heartbeat.fallbacks` as the public sibling config contract for heartbeat-specific fallback chains and strict `[]` heartbeat runs?
rationale: The PR intentionally adds a new config/default and fallback-policy surface, and repository policy treats these as compatibility-sensitive even when the implementation preserves existing defaults.

options.title: Accept sibling heartbeat fallbacks
options.body: Approve `heartbeat.fallbacks` after the docs-format fix because it preserves unset behavior and reuses the existing per-run fallback override boundary.

options.title: Choose a different config shape
options.body: Ask the branch to switch to object-form `heartbeat.model` or another explicit policy surface before merge.

options.title: Defer heartbeat-specific policy
options.body: Pause or close the PR if maintainers do not want a new heartbeat-scoped fallback setting in core right now.

recommendation.title: Accept sibling heartbeat fallbacks
recommendation.body: Approve `heartbeat.fallbacks` after the docs-format fix because it preserves unset behavior and reuses the existing per-run fallback override boundary.
